## Summary

The November 7, 2026 guide marks the Web Elements Payment Request Button deprecated and unsupported in Stripe.js Endive or later. It continues to work in earlier Stripe.js versions for as long as those versions are supported. Stripe recommends migrating to Express Checkout Element, or using another preferred Link integration such as Contact Details Element or Payment Element.

## Version and migration

- **May 8, 2026.** Stripe already advised against using the Payment Request Button in Web Elements and named Link Authentication Element, Express Checkout Element and Payment Element.
- **Endive.** The September 30, 2026 changelog says `elements.create('paymentRequestButton')` throws starting with Endive and React integrations rendering `PaymentRequestButtonElement` are affected. It names versions through Dahlia as retaining the Element. The November Link guide qualifies this by continued earlier-version support. This cutoff applies to the Web Elements runtime. See [[stripe-express-checkout-element]] for the separate package declarations and React wrapper changes.
- **Preferred routes.** The November migration capture indexes Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents variants. The full April 21, 2026 Payment Intents migration requires integrations using the Charges API with tokens to migrate to Payment Intents first. See [[source-stripe-express-checkout-element-migration]]. The separate November Contact Details guide calls it the former Link Authentication Element and documents a distinct email-collection and Link authentication flow ahead of Payment Element.

## Existing integrations on supported pre-Endive Stripe.js

- **Customer and authentication flow.** A customer new to the merchant can already have saved Link payment details. Returning Link customers click the Link button and enter an SMS or email code. Link then loads their saved payment details for one-click checkout. If they authenticated at this merchant or another Link-enabled business in the previous 90 days, they can skip reauthentication. A customer new to Link is prompted to save their information when clicking Link. Authentication, credential loading and the one-click option do not establish a successful charge.
- **Features and settings.** The guides describe compatibility with existing card features such as subscriptions, no additional Link fees, and on/off control through payment method settings. These details apply to this legacy client Element.
- **Connect.** Link is automatically available to connected accounts accessing the supported Payment Request Button through a Connect platform integration. The platform manages Link for payments it processes. For payments processed independently, the connected account manages Link through payment method settings in its own Dashboard. The captures specify no Connect charge type.

New raw lines 5-17 explicitly mark it deprecated and unsupported in Stripe.js Endive or later. It continues to work in earlier Stripe.js versions only as long as those versions are supported. November recommends migration to Express Checkout Element or using another preferred Element such as Contact Details or Payment Element. On the supported legacy browser route, a person new to the merchant can already have a Link account and pay with saved details. Returning Link customers click Link and authenticate with an SMS or email code, then Link loads their saved payment details. Prior authentication within 90 days at this or another Link-enabled business can skip reauthentication. A customer new to Link is prompted to save details. Both old raw lines 10-19 and new raw lines 15-24 retain payment method settings, compatibility with card features including subscriptions and no additional Link fees. Both old raw lines 21-26 and new raw lines 26-31 say connected accounts accessing the Element via a platform get Link automatically, the platform manages the settings for payments processed through it, and the connected account manages the setting for independent payments via its own Dashboard. The candidate for source-stripe-payment-request-button-link.md preserves the original 90-day and Connect details and adds the explicit cutoff, revised alternatives and normal returning SMS/email flow. Authentication, loaded payment credentials and the ability to make a one-click payment do not show that a payment succeeded.
payments-link-payment-request-button-lin.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-request-button-link, old raw lines 4-12 and new raw lines 5-17 show the substantive integration change in the captured guidance: the May no-longer-recommended Web Elements path and its Link Authentication, Express Checkout and Payment Element alternatives become an explicit Stripe.js Endive-and-later support cutoff in November, earlier supported Stripe.js versions retain the Element, and the guide directs migration to Express Checkout or another preferred Element such as Contact Details or Payment Element. The 2026-09-30 Endive changelog, captured November 7, confirms that elements.create('paymentRequestButton') throws starting with Endive, React PaymentRequestButtonElement integrations are affected, and Stripe.js through Dahlia retains the Element (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-deprecate-payment-request-button-2026-11-07.md lines 5-17). Keep the May 8, 2026 wording and legacy provenance dated in source-stripe-payment-request-button-link.md lines 13-17 and in the reciprocal Link concept section. The separate Contact Details guide identifies the former Link Authentication name and a distinct checkout/email flow. Add reciprocal compatibility context to the Express Checkout migration route, whose November capture is only Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents navigation. The separately captured April full Payment Intents migration requires Charges API with tokens integrations to migrate to Payment Intents first. The old and new See also links are navigation and the CDN/alt-text/whitespace edits are presentational. Old raw lines 17-26 and new raw lines 22-31 retain the authentication and Connect behavior conditionally for the supported legacy client Element. The cutoff does not imply removal of stripe.paymentRequest() or a server API change. The platform manages Link for payments it processes and connected accounts manage the setting for independent payments through their Dashboard.
